angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 758,313 km at 113.55 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.8064 +/- 0.0172 mas (same row, RUWE 0.85): 113.55 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.09 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Luque et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-292 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...623A.114L/abstract): 758,313 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Luque et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-292 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...623A.114L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5725 +/- 65 K from Luque et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-292 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...623A.114L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Luque et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-292 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019A&A...623A.114L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-292.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.363, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
